instruction.text: Complete the image of a Roman fort.

atoms.b: As they advanced and retreated, the Romans built many forts, or castra, to ((++control lose)) their territory and keep watch of the Picts.
Roman forts had tall ((++towers powers)) called turrets built into the wall, along with a ((++ditch witch)) in front of the outer walls to help protect against attacking tribes.

text: Thanks to their strong, stone foundations, the layouts of many Roman forts in Scotland can still be seen today!

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Along both Hadrian’s Wall and the Antonine Wall, the Romans built smaller forts called milecastles. These were placed about a mile apart to guard the walls and control movement across the frontier.
Larger Roman forts could house up to 600 soldiers, but milecastles usually only held about 30. Inside, there were barracks where soldiers slept, ate and carried out their daily duties.

atoms.a: Along which two frontiers were milecastles built?
How many soldiers lived in a Roman milecastle?

instruction.text: Drag the three gifts the Romans might have left for their gods.

feedback.finish: Some soldiers served on the wall for years, so milecastles had temples where they could pray to Roman gods.

instruction.text: Select all the foods that do not belong on a Roman soldier’s table.

feedback.finish: Near the forts on Hadrian’s Wall, Roman soldiers grew some grain for making bread. However, they depended mostly on food brought in through trade, such as olive oil, meat and wine.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in the Roman soldier’s letter.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: The Romans often wrote letters on thin pieces of wood, called tabellae, which were an everyday way to send messages before paper became common.

atoms.b: I’m holding up well here on the northern ((++frontier farm)). Fortunately, my new role as ((++bathhouse zoo)) keeper keeps me away from guard duty.
The merchants bring cartloads of bread, meat, ((++oil bananas)) and other goods, so we are well fed. Of course, all traders are checked and ((++taxed captured)) when passing through the gates!

It’s freezing so far ((++north south)), but I have enough warm ((++clothes cloths)), so I am getting by! Although, if it’s not too much trouble, would you be able to send me some more underpants? I’ve run out!

feedback.finish: Archaeologists have uncovered lots of Roman letters near Hadrian’s Wall, revealing what life was like on the northern frontier. The letter you’ve just read is based on one of these!
